summary: Florida Forest Service 100-ft lookout tower on US 41 in Collier County, ready by April 1964; no source found for its later history.

events.note: Construction under way in February 1964 with about 80 feet erected; ready for use by early April 1964.
Opening day, a Friday: tower to be open to visitors all day; the first 100 climbers were to receive certificates.

evidence.supports: Construction under way in February 1964, about 80 feet erected
evidence.quote: Construction work on the Marco fire tower is under way and about 80 feet of the tower has already been erected.

evidence.supports: Florida Forest Service; first of three fire towers planned for Collier County
evidence.quote: The Florida Forest Service tomorrow will unveil the first of three fire towers planned for Collier County.

evidence.supports: 100-foot tower ready for use, about 16 miles southeast of Naples on US 41
evidence.quote: the 100-foot lookout tower now ready for use about 16 miles southeast of Naples on U.S. 41

evidence.supports: Same clipping places the tower east of Naples
evidence.quote: The tower just completed east of Naples

evidence.supports: Planned opening-day visitor access; first 100 climbers to receive Towernaut certificates
evidence.quote: will be open to visitors all day Friday, with the first 100 people to climb the tower receiving 'Towernaut' certificates

corrections.why: T51S-R27E is a township and range land description printed on the page, not an agency. The April 1964 clipping names the Florida Forest Service.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The clipping says both about 16 miles southeast of Naples on US 41 and east of Naples. The story gives the mileage and notes that the direction is described two ways.

sources.title: Marco - Forest Lookouts (1964 clippings from The Daily News)

notes_for_editor: Single source: a fan transcription of two 1964 newspaper items. Nothing found on staffing, fires, fate or today's status. Neither the NHLR nor the FFLOS Florida list (checked 2026-10-21) includes Marco. Brief agency value was a land description and is corrected. Height rests on the clipping's 100-foot figure.
